To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the sample size calculations and analysis methods in cluster-based studies of clinical decision support systems are not adequate and that there is a need for a standard methodological guideline for the planning and reporting of such studies.

(1) cluster-based studies are not adequately addressed in reports; (2) the intracluster correlation coefficient is a useful parameter in sample size calculations for future studies; and (3) the analysis of cluster-based studies should take into account the clustering effect.

None of the 24 studies of CDSSs that were identified by our review included sample size calculations to account for clustering, while only 14 (58.3%) took account of the cluster effect in the analysis.".
